protections: Only an authenticated user who supplies a defined ComponentId they are entitled to (member of the component, or non-member of a publicFiles=yes storage component) may receive a file from FileServer (core-war/src/main/java/org/silverpeas/web/servlets/FileServer.java:80-91, FileServer.java:148-164).

The path that is finally opened must resolve inside the directory the request is entitled to (component upload repository, temporary repository, or a server-chosen attachment path), never to an arbitrary absolute path and never through '..' segments (FileServer.java:108-134, core-library/src/main/java/org/silverpeas/core/io/file/SilverpeasFileProvider.java:202-216).

Every file-serving servlet authenticates the caller and authorises the addressed component or document before streaming bytes (FileServer.java:84; core-war/src/main/java/org/silverpeas/web/servlets/TempFileServer.java:51, 77-79; contrast core-war/src/main/java/org/silverpeas/web/servlets/OnlineFileServer.java:58-99, which has neither).
Server-side scanners that turn FileServer URLs into DataSources must not resolve files the scanned content's author is not entitled to (FileServer.java:178-191).

traps.reason_to_dismiss: The allow-branch is commented 'Personal space', so a request without ComponentId reads as a deliberate, supported personal-space access rather than as a missing check; and the framework's own controller also authorises a null componentId, so 'use the standard access controller' looks like a complete fix.

Once a ComponentId the caller may access is present the remaining path is treated as trusted data written by the application, and TypeUpload/DirType/Directory look like internal flags of the shipped URL builders (core-library/src/main/java/org/silverpeas/core/util/file/FileServerUtils.java:117-153, FileServerUtils.java:240-246); the advisory reads as the missing-ComponentId case rather than as a missing containment check. Sharing a guard with T4 also looks tempting because one 'path resolved under the repository' rule appears to cover both.

It is the legacy inline-media servlet, not the FileServer servlet the report names, and its documentId/attachmentId branches look like the only interesting ones; the fallback branch (line 93-96) reaches the same SilverpeasFileProvider sink with no session check, no component authorisation and no path validation at all.

The servlet already carries an explicit security check named isValid() and requires an authenticated session through SilverpeasAuthenticatedHttpServlet, so it presents as the one sibling that already did the job; the check is in fact a two-substring test that never looks at path traversal.

Nothing looks missing here: publicFiles=yes is a documented per-component file-storage mode, so the branch reads as a feature to keep. The over-hardening trap is that the obvious repair of the access-control gap (route every request through isComponentAvailableToUser, line 159-160, or replace isUserAllowed wholesale) deletes this branch and silently denies every non-member of a storage component.

It is a programmatic content scanner, not a user-facing HTTP route: it processes WYSIWYG HTML already authored inside the application during mail generation, so the parameters look like app-generated links and the absence of any session, ComponentId or access check goes unnoticed.

masking: T2 is only reachable on FileServer once T1's gate is passed: the undefined-ComponentId allow (FileServer.java:150-152) and the unconfined path resolution (FileServer.java:120-121, 129-131 -> SilverpeasFileProvider.java:208-212) must both hold, so repairing T1 alone leaves the absolute-path and '..' reads available to any user who can name a component they may access (every public / publicFiles component).

Once the TypeUpload absolute branch is removed, '..' segments in Directory/Size/SourceFile (FileServer.java:113-117, 129-131) and the DirType=temporary branch (FileServer.java:123-127) become the remaining ways out of the entitled directory, i.e. the relative shape only becomes visible after the absolute shape is fixed.
T3 and T4 are only reachable as separate code paths because neither shares a guard with FileServer; a fix written only inside FileServer.getSilverpeasFile cannot mask them.

conflicts.what: The natural repair of the missing-ComponentId gap is to route everything through isComponentAvailableToUser (FileServer.java:159-160) or to delegate to ComponentAccessController; applied unconditionally it denies the publicFiles=yes storage components that must remain downloadable by any logged-in non-member (FileServer.java:154-157, DefaultInstanceAccessControlExtension.java:72-74, ComponentAccessControllerTest.java:176-177).

Closing the path-containment gap in the shared provider (SilverpeasFileProvider.java:202-216) by forbidding absolute descriptors breaks the legitimate absolute attachment paths OnlineFileServer.java:76-91 depends on, so the containment rule cannot simply live in the shared layer; it has to be per call-site, which is what keeps T2 and T3 independent.

A single 'resolved path must start with the uploads repository' rule reused by TempFileServer breaks that servlet's legitimate files, which live under the temporary repository joined at TempFileServer.java:81-82, not under the component upload path.

fairness_risks: publicFiles=yes legitimately lets any logged-in user who is NOT a member of the storage component download its files (FileServer.java:154-157); a security rule of the form 'require membership of the component' contradicts a documented behaviour and would fail a must-keep-working test.

Absolute path descriptors are legitimate for attachments: OnlineFileServer.java:76-91 and core-war/src/main/java/org/silverpeas/web/servlets/RestOnlineFileServer.java:167-173 deliberately build them from database rows; a blanket ban on absolute paths in SilverpeasFileProvider refuses an input shape a legitimate use needs.

The Size parameter is a legitimate resized-image directory marker produced by FileServerUtils.getImageURL (FileServerUtils.java:193-197) and used for thumbnails; rejecting every Size value, rather than validating/normalising it, breaks thumbnail serving.

TempFileServer must keep serving nested and non-ASCII names under the temporary repository (core-library/src/test/java/org/silverpeas/core/util/FileServerUtilsTest.java:62-67); a rule that forbids path separators outright, rather than traversal, would break it.

Requiring a defined ComponentId refuses requests that the pinned code serves as 'Personal space' (FileServer.java:150-152); that is the published intent, but any hidden test that still expects a personal-space URL without ComponentId to work would contradict the security rule.

design.why: Five independent judgements at five different fix sites with five different reasons to leave them alone: (T1) the undefined-ComponentId allow, which is dismissed as an intentional 'Personal space' feature and which even the framework controller (ComponentAccessController.java:145-149) would keep; (T2) no containment of the resolved path at all, dismissed because a caller with a ComponentId is already authorised and because TypeUpload/DirType look like internal URL-builder flags; (T3) a sibling servlet in the same package that reaches the same SilverpeasFileProvider sink with no authentication, no component authorisation and no path validation, dismissed as 'the legacy servlet, not the one the report names'; (T4) a sibling servlet that presents as already protected because it has isValid() and a session, but whose check is a two-substring test that never looks at '..'; and (T5) the coupled publicFiles=yes storage mode that the natural over-broad access-control repair destroys. That gives four deepseek-type traps (protection absent, each with its own dismissal) and one mimo-type coupled value (T5), spread over FileServer.java, TempFileServer.java, OnlineFileServer.java and the shared SilverpeasFileProvider/descriptor pair, so no single guard closes more than one. T6 (the ImageUrlToDataSourceScanner, which resolves FileServer parameters into mail attachments with no access check) is a good optional sixth when the harness can drive MailContentProcess, but it is same-file and mail-generation-bound, so it adds less than T3/T4 and risks an unfair test surface. T2 deliberately folds the absolute-path (TypeUpload), the temporary-repository (DirType) and the '..' (Directory/Size/SourceFile) shapes into one trap because a single containment guard at FileServer.getSilverpeasFile closes all three; splitting them would inflate the count.
